title: Why Making Things Harder Makes Better Buyers
hook_text: MAKING SOMETHING HARDER TO BUY BRINGS BETTER BUYERS

beats.say: You spent weeks building an offer, but your sign-up form gets 100 dead leads a week.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a solitary figure walking across a wet concrete plaza at blue hour.

beats.say: How do you stop wasting time on buyers who never buy?
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a massive steel bridge underpass cutting through grey fog.

beats.say: Most people think you need to make checkout faster and easier to grow your customer list.
beats.visual: Close up of worn hands sliding a plain metal latch on an old wooden door.

beats.say: That assumption costs you thousands in wasted support calls and refunds from the wrong crowd.
beats.visual: High angle shot of heavy rain striking dark asphalt in a narrow alley.

beats.say: Here is the friction dial: adding steps and questions cuts total volume.
beats.visual: Extreme close up of a heavy brass key turning slowly in a dark lock.

beats.say: Why would you intentionally turn away potential sign-ups?
beats.visual: Silhouette of a person standing on a windy concrete rooftop against gray clouds.

beats.say: Because it filters out tire kickers and leaves only the buyers who actually value the result.
beats.visual: Single practical light cutting through deep shadows in an empty brick warehouse.

beats.say: About 1 in 5 US businesses close by year five, often drowning in poor customers.
beats.visual: Wide shot of rusting industrial pipes running along a damp stone wall.

beats.say: Instead of removing friction from the start, you add hoops once your flow works.
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a heavy steel door bolted shut in a concrete wall.

beats.say: You trade raw volume for high intent by forcing questions before checkout.
beats.visual: Extreme close up of heavy iron chain links resting on wet gravel.

beats.say: That exact friction sweet spot protects your time and raises your average order quality.
beats.visual: Blue hour wide shot of an empty highway bridge stretching into fog.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: Single sodium light glowing through heavy mist on a dark suburban road.

caption: Making something harder to buy can bring better buyers. #MoneyPsychology #BusinessRules #QuietMoney #WealthBuilding #Entrepreneurship
description: Adding friction and questions to your offer cuts low-quality volume and attracts better buyers. Here is how to find the sweet spot.
first_comment: What is the hardest step in your current offer?

facts.claim: About 1 in 5 US businesses close in their first year and close to half by year five
facts.basis: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Business Employment Dynamics
